post.description:
Supply exactly one of templateId or customText. Style fields override the template, which overrides the system defaults. Produced in the background: poll the job, then fetch its result. Send an Idempotency-Key header so a repeated click returns the same job instead of producing a second copy. Naming a versionId needs dvc.view-version-history.view as well.

The copy is always in the ORIGINAL's format - nothing is converted, and the original is never modified. Supported: PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), JPEG and PNG. Anything else, including legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt, is a 415.

pageScope=first-page-only means something different in each format, because "page" does: PDF - page 1; Word - page 1, which is done by turning on the section's title page (its existing first-page header content is preserved); Excel - the first VISIBLE worksheet, since a spreadsheet has no pages until it is printed; PowerPoint - slide 1; images - the whole image, which is one page by definition.

Known limitations. (1) In Word, Excel and PowerPoint the watermark is an ordinary picture, so a recipient who opens the file can delete it; Phase 1 makes provenance visible, it does not make it tamper-proof. (2) The in-app preview may not show the mark - check the downloaded file in desktop Office or LibreOffice. (3) In Excel the mark floats ABOVE the cells (Excel offers nothing behind them), which is why opacity has a floor; a floating picture in desktop Excel can also take the click when somebody selects a cell underneath it, so a recipient may need to click past it or drag it aside to edit those cells. (4) A JPEG copy is re-encoded and loses EXIF metadata, including GPS. (5) A digitally signed document is refused with 422 - any change would break its signature. (6) Password-protected files are refused with 422.

get.description: Unlike GET /{userId}/platform-roles below - which tenant-admin screens use to inspect some *other* user and deliberately excludes PLATFORM_ADMIN, see KeycloakUserService#PLATFORM_ROLE_NAMES for why - this is always the caller asking about themselves, so PLATFORM_ADMIN is included here. Read directly off the authorities already derived from the caller's own validated JWT for this request (see AuthorizationService#myPlatformRoles), not a Keycloak admin lookup. This is what the frontend calls to decide whether to show platform-admin-only screens, such as Permission Catalog create/edit/delete.

get.description: These are Keycloak-only realm roles, never rows in the roles/user_roles tables - see GET /{userId}/roles (UserRoleController) for tenant-defined DMS roles instead.
